dhp360:1: Restraint of eye is good, restraint of ear is good,
dhp360:4: restraint of nose is good, restraint of tongue is good,
dhp361:1: restraint of body is good, restraint of speech is good,
dhp361:4: restraint of mind is good, restraint is everywhere good,
dhp361:5: a monastic who is restrained everywhere is liberated from all suffering.
dhp362:1: One who controls his hands, controls his feet,
dhp362:2: controls his speech, controls the (mind) supreme,
dhp362:4: solitary, content: that one is called a monastic.
dhp363:1: That monastic who restrains the mouth, who speaks well, and who is modest,
dhp363:3: who explains the meaning of the Dhamma, his speech is sweet.
dhp364:2: The one who finds pleasure in the Dhamma, delights in Dhamma, reflects on Dhamma,
dhp364:3: the monastic who remembers Dhamma, does not abandon the Good Dhamma.
dhp365:1: One should not despise one’s own gains, one should not live envious of others,
dhp365:3: the monastic who is envious of others does not attain concentration.
dhp366:1: Even if a monastic gains little he should not despise his gains,
dhp366:4: even the very gods praise the one of pure life who is diligent.
dhp367:2: The one who does not have fondness at all for mind and body,
dhp367:4: and who grieves not for what does not exist, is surely called a monastic.
dhp368:1: That monastic who dwells in loving-kindness, with faith in Buddha’s dispensation,
dhp368:3: should attain the state of peace, the joy in stilling of (all) conditions.
dhp369:1: Please bail out this boat, monastic, when bailed out it will go lightly,
dhp369:3: cutting off passion and hatred, from here one will go to Nibbāna.
dhp370:2: One should cut off five, one should abandon five, one should cultivate five more,
dhp370:3: the monastic who surmounts five attachments is called a flood-crosser.
dhp371:1: Meditate, monastic, do not be heedless,
dhp371:2: do not let your mind swirl around in strands of desire,
dhp371:3: do not, heedless, swallow a (hot) iron ball,
dhp371:4: do not, while burning, cry: ‘This is suffering.’
dhp372:1: There is no concentration for one without wisdom, there is no wisdom for one without concentration,
dhp372:3: the one who has both concentration and wisdom is indeed in the presence of Nibbāna.
dhp373:2: For the one who has entered an empty place, a monastic with a peaceful mind,
dhp373:4: there is superhuman delight from insight into true Dhamma.
dhp374:2: Whoever has right mindfulness regarding the rise and fall of the components (of mind and body)
dhp374:3: gains joy and happiness, that is the deathless state for the one who knows.
dhp375:2: This is the very beginning for the wise monastic here:
dhp375:3: contentment, guarding the senses, and restraint in the regulations.
dhp376:1: One should resort to spiritual friends, ones of pure life, ones who are diligent,
dhp376:3: one should be of friendly disposition, one who will be skilful in his conduct,
dhp376:6: rejoicing frequently because of that, one will make an end to suffering.
dhp377:1: Just as striped jasmine casts off its withered flowers,
dhp377:4: so, monastics, cast off (all) passion and hatred.
dhp378:2: Calm in body and calm in speech, having calmness and composure,
dhp378:3: having thrown off worldly gain the monastic is called one at peace.
dhp379:1: By oneself one should censure self, by oneself one should be controlled,
dhp379:4: he who guards himself, mindful, will live happily, monastic.
dhp380:1: Self is the protector of self, self is the refuge of self,
dhp380:5: therefore one should restrain oneself, as a merchant his noble horse.
dhp381:1: The monastic, having much happiness, with faith in the dispensation of the Buddha,
dhp381:3: could attain to the state of peace, happy in the stilling of (all) conditions.
dhp382:1: That young monastic who is devoted to the Buddha’s dispensation,
dhp382:4: shines forth in this world, like the moon freed from a cloud.
dhp382:5: The Chapter about Monastics, the Twenty-Fifth
